You are doing a REUSE-angle code review of an uncommitted change in the repo at /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. Do NOT edit anything. Do NOT hunt for correctness bugs. Only report reuse problems in the CHANGED code.

Get the exact diff under review by running:
cd /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim && git --no-pager diff HEAD -- src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp tests/hybrid/program_buffer.test.cpp tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp tests/hybrid/state_drain.test.cpp tests/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.test.cpp

Context: this change rewrites the V-register Program-Buffer sweep (`pb_v_data_sweep` in src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp) to use RVV LMUL=8 grouping (4 grouped vle8.v/vse8.v cover all 32 registers in ONE PB execution), and repacks the shared scratch region to vlenb stride in the stager (`stage_v_to_scratch`/`read_v_from_scratch` in src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp). Callers in resume_driver.hpp/state_drain.hpp lost the `stride` argument. Tests updated across 4 files.

Your REUSE job: flag NEW code that re-implements something the codebase already has:
- The new `kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u` constant -- is there an existing vtype builder/constant it duplicates? Grep src/hybrid.
- The packing loops in stage_v_to_scratch/read_v_from_scratch -- do they duplicate an existing byte-marshalling helper?
- The new `staged_gpr_value` test helper in program_buffer.test.cpp -- does it duplicate logic already in recording_bus.hpp, test_helpers.hpp, or the sibling test files (resume_driver.test.cpp scans the DMI op stream similarly)?
- Any magic constant (8 for LMUL, 32 registers) that has an existing named constant.

Return a short list: file:line, one-line summary, concrete cost (what is duplicated + which existing thing to use). If clean on this angle, say so plainly.

content.text: Let me look at the complete v_regfile_xfer.hpp file to understand the constants:

content.content:
1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header
9	// provides the matching host-side copy:
10	//
11	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
12	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
13	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
14	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so the drained v0..v31 land in state.vreg[]
15	//     (the handoff file).
16	//
17	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
18	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
19	// the reference fixture.
20	//
21	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
22	
23	#pragma once
24	
25	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
26	
27	#include <cstddef>
28	#include <cstdint>
29	#include <cstring>
30	#include <span>
31	#include <stdexcept>
32	
33	namespace hybrid
34	{
35	
36	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to the
37	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
38	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
39	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
40	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
41	
42	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
43	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
44	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
45	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
46	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
47	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
48	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
49	  -> uint64_t
50	{
51	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
52	}
53	
54	// Sentinel for "no V scratch configured". ResumeDriver/StateDrain default to
55	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
56	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
57	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
58	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
59	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);
60	
61	namespace detail
62	{
63	
64	// Byte offset of the scratch region inside a RAM span: its top page. Throws
65	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
66	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
67	{
68	  if (ram_size < kVScratchBytes)
69	    throw std::runtime_error(
70	      "v_regfile_xfer: RAM span smaller than the V scratch page");
71	  return ram_size - kVScratchBytes;
72	}
73	
74	}  // namespace detail
75	
76	// Copy state.vreg[] into the span's top scratch page. Called just before vsim
77	// resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from scratch and pick up QEMU 1's
78	// V values.
79	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
80	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
81	{
82	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
83	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
84	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
85	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
86	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
87	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
88	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
89	}
90	
91	// Copy the span's top scratch page into state.vreg[]. Called inside the vsim
92	// drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has settled the (possibly
93	// mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
94	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
95	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
96	{
97	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
98	  // Unpack the vlenb-packed scratch back into the wire-strided vreg[] slots.
99	  // Each slot's padding (bytes vlenb..HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) is left as-is:
100	  // callers pass a passthrough state whose padding is already zero (the QEMU
101	  // drain zero-fills it), so the full 128-byte slots stay byte-identical to the
102	  // oracle that --verify compares against.
103	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
104	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
105	    std::memcpy(state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
106	                ram.data() + off + r * vlenb, vlenb);
107	}
108	
109	}  // namespace hybrid

- **File**: `tests/hybrid/program_buffer.test.cpp:258-268`
- **Summary**: New test helper that extracts a staged 64-bit GPR value by scanning `bus.writes` for abstract-command writes
- **Duplication**: Identical pattern already exists inline in `tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp:980-990` as the nested `x7_gpa_staged` lambda that performs the same write-sequence scan (kData0/kData1 preceding kCommand with write bit set)

The program_buffer version is generic (extracts for any GPR `g`); resume_driver uses a hardcoded inline check for x7. Extracting a shared helper (`extract_abstract_write_value` in test_helpers.hpp or similar) would eliminate the duplication and improve test maintainability across the test suite.

- **`kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u`**: No existing vtype builder or constant — this is a legitimate new constant (clean).

- **`kRegsPerGroup = 8` and loop step-by-8**: Locally scoped, explicit, and clear. No magic number duplication (clean).
